name: Call the DD Regional Office (first call for DD services)

summary.plain: The DD Regional Office is the front door to Missouri services for developmental disabilities. Call it first.
summary.pro: A referral to the DMH Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) Springfield Regional Office or Joplin Satellite Office starts intake for eligibility under 9 CSR 45-2.010.

who.plain: It is for any age. Anyone can make the referral: family, a friend, a school, or a doctor. Only the person, or the person's guardian or other responsible person, signs the application. You do not need Medicaid.
who.pro: Any person may refer. Only the applicant or the applicant's responsible person may complete the formal application. MO HealthNet is not required for eligibility. The office must give application forms by the end of the next business day after any inquiry, and must contact the person if no application arrives within 30 calendar days (9 CSR 45-2.010(4)(B)).

plain: Find the office for your county in the list below.
Call the office, or fill in the online referral form.
Ask for Intake.
Tell Intake about the disability and how the person communicates.
Sign the application packet when it comes.
Send the packet back within 2 months, or the referral closes.
pro: Refer online (DDD REDCap referral form), by phone, fax, email, mail, or in person. Referral data: name, date of birth, Medicaid number if any, disability, communication needs, addresses, responsible person and referrer details.
Intake contacts the family within 1 business day of a complete referral (DDD Referral and Application Process, 12 Mar 2024).

Return the signed packet within 2 months or the referral becomes inactive. Forms: application, Authorization for Disclosure of Consumer Medical-Health Information, Authorized Representative form, Notice of Privacy Practices receipt, Application Acknowledgment form.
Then follow the DMH DD eligibility record for records, rule time limits, and appeal rights.

bring: The person's name, birth date, and Social Security number
MO HealthNet (Medicaid) number, if any
The name of the disability and who diagnosed it
Guardianship or custody court papers, if any

wait.plain: Intake should call you within 1 business day of a complete referral.
wait.pro: Intake contact within 1 business day of a complete referral (DDD sheet, 2024). Forms by the end of the next business day after an inquiry (9 CSR 45-2.010(4)(B)).

plain: Many families do not know this office exists. It serves adults too, not only children.
Call the office for your county. The Joplin office serves 11 of the 23 counties.
The referral closes if the packet is not back within 2 months.
pro: Springfield street address ZIP is 65802. Mail goes to PO Box 5030, Springfield, MO 65801-5030. The DDD directory ZIP 65810 is wrong (fact check, 27 Oct 2026).
Joplin street address ZIP is 64801 (state facility record). DMH prints 64802, a PO box ZIP. Confirm the mailing address with the office.
The DMH office page spells Stone County as Stoney (typo).

appeal.plain: If the office says no, you can appeal. See DMH DD eligibility.
appeal.pro: Appeals under 9 CSR 45-2.020. See the DMH DD eligibility record and the appeals table.

summary.plain: Family navigators who have lived it help you find your way. The help is free.

name: DMH Developmental Disabilities (DD) eligibility

summary.plain: DD eligibility opens the door to Missouri DD services. It comes before support coordination, DD waivers, and most county DD help.
summary.pro: Eligibility for DMH Division of Developmental Disabilities services under RSMo 630.005 and 9 CSR 45-2.010 (amended effective 30 Apr 2023). It is the prerequisite for support coordination, DD waivers, SWMAP, and most SB40 board services.

who.plain: A person of any age may qualify. The disability must start before age 22, or before 18 for intellectual disability. It must be likely to last for life. An adult must need a lot of help in at least 2 life areas. The areas are self-care, communication, learning, moving around, making decisions, and living on their own or working. You do not need Medicaid.
who.pro: RSMo 630.005: a condition attributable to intellectual disability, cerebral palsy, epilepsy, head injury, autism, a learning disability related to brain dysfunction, or any other mental or physical impairment; manifested before age 22 (intellectual disability before 18); likely to continue indefinitely; substantial functional limitations in 2 or more of 6 areas (self-care, receptive and expressive language, learning, self-direction, capacity for independent living or economic self-sufficiency, mobility); need for individually planned and coordinated services. 9 CSR 45-2.010(3): ages 5 to 17, MAAS 1.5 SD below the mean in 2 areas or 2 SD below in 1 area; adults 18 and older, substantial limits (2 SD) in 2 or more areas (DDD sheet: at least 95% below average in TWO areas). There is no one-area route for adults. If the claim is intellectual disability and the MAAS shows fewer than 2 areas, DDD must consider other assessments the applicant provides (9 CSR 45-2.010(4)(E)). MO HealthNet is not required.

plain: Call the Regional Office for your county, or use the online referral form.
Send back the signed application packet within 2 months.
Gather school, medical, and test records that show the disability started before age 22.
If Social Security made a disability decision, send its form SSA-831.
Take part in the MAAS video interview if DDD sets one up.
Read the decision letter. Write down the date on it.
pro: Refer online, by phone, fax, email, mail, or in person. Intake contacts the family within 1 business day; the packet is due within 2 months.
DDD requests records about 5 business days after the paperwork returns. Records can take 3 months or more (DDD Referral and Application Process, 2024).

Useful records: IEP and IEP Evaluation Report, 504 plan, First Steps record, IQ and psychological tests, adaptive behavior assessments, genetic or neurological tests, SSA-831 (DDD cannot use the SSA Benefit Verification Letter), guardianship or custody orders.

DDD accepts a valid adaptive assessment from the last 3 years in place of a new MAAS (DDD Intake MAAS sheet; DDD practice, not a rule). The MAAS is by video: about 30 minutes with the person and 60 with an informant; results in about 5 business days.
If the decision is slow, cite the 9 CSR 45-2.010(4) time limits in writing (see How long).

bring: IEP and the latest school evaluation report
504 plan or First Steps records, if any
IQ tests, psychological reports, and adaptive behavior tests
Medical records, for example genetic or neurology tests
Social Security form SSA-831, if SSA made a disability decision
Guardianship or custody court orders, if any

wait.plain: Getting old records can take 3 months or more. After DDD has enough records, the rule gives it 30 business days to decide. You can ask DDD about this deadline.
wait.pro: 9 CSR 45-2.010(4): comprehensive evaluation within 30 business days after a valid application and sufficient records; up to 5 more business days when all information is in hand ((4)(H)); up to 30 more business days under a temporary action plan only when records are still missing ((4)(G)). Eligibility notice within 3 business days of the decision. ISP within 30 business days after eligibility, or 5 business days for immediate need. The DDD MAAS sheet allows itself 60 business days after records arrive; the rule controls (fact check, 27 Oct 2026). Reassessment needs 60 calendar days written notice and a 60-day discharge plan.

plain: Adults need a lot of help in at least 2 life areas. One area is not enough.
Adults diagnosed late may lack childhood records. Ask schools and doctors for old records early.
DDD cannot use the Social Security benefit letter. It needs form SSA-831.
The MAAS is done by video. If you have no device, ask to use one at the Regional Office, a library, or the school.
DD eligibility does not mean a waiver. DD waivers need a lot of help in 3 life areas.
pro: Adults: 2 or more areas (9 CSR 45-2.010(3)(C)). File 01 misread the DDD sheet as allowing one area; the fact check corrected this.
Waiver ICF/IID level of care needs 3 or more areas (DD Waiver Eligibility sheet 09/2024; DD Waiver Manual 1.1).
A person found eligible before can usually re-open without new records or a new MAAS, unless legal status changed (Re-Establishing Division Services, 30 Sep 2024).
The rule screens out at screening only a person whose disability clearly was not manifested before 22.

appeal.plain: You can appeal a no. Tell the Regional Office within 30 days of the date on the letter, by phone or in writing. If the person gets services now, they continue during the appeal. If you hire a lawyer, tell the Regional Office within 10 days. Missouri Protection and Advocacy helps for free at 1-800-392-8667.
appeal.pro: 9 CSR 45-2.020: written notice on a DMH form at least 30 calendar days before the action. Step 1: appeal to regional office staff, verbally or in writing, within 30 calendar days (the rule counts from receipt, the DDD sheet from the notice; use the notice date, the shorter period); regional director decides within 10 business days. Step 2: request an appeals referee within 30 calendar days of that decision; 30 days notice; hearing within 60 calendar days; the regional office has the burden of proof; decision within 30 calendar days of the hearing. Step 3: judicial review under RSMo Chapter 536. Counsel must notify the head of the regional office within 10 calendar days of being retained (9 CSR 45-2.020(3)(C)6.A); the DDD sheet says 10 business days; use the shorter period. No reduction or termination of services until appeals are exhausted ((3)(E)). Time limits are liberally interpreted ((2)(A)).

name: DD support coordination (case management)

summary.plain: A support coordinator helps a DD-eligible person make a service plan each year. Only the support coordinator can ask for waiver funding.
summary.pro: Targeted Case Management (TCM) by DDD staff or a contracted SB40 board or nonprofit. The coordinator writes the Person-Centered Service Plan (ISP), links services, and submits the plan, budget, and PON to Utilization Review.

who.plain: People found eligible by DMH DD. With MO HealthNet, the person gets a support coordinator in every county. Without MO HealthNet, it depends on the county. Some counties give a local helper. Others give a state phone line.
who.pro: Active MO HealthNet: Support Coordination (TCM) in every county. No MO HealthNet: Division Resource and Referral (Information Specialist, 1-800-241-2741) in Greene, Henry, Laclede, Ozark, Stone, and Taney; Provider Resource and Referral (County Support Specialist) in Barry, Barton, Cedar, Christian, Dade, Dallas, Douglas, Hickory, Jasper, Lawrence, McDonald, Newton, Polk, St. Clair, Vernon, Webster, and Wright (DDD Division Services sheet, 14 Mar 2024; county contracts can change). DDD: new requests for funding require active Medicaid; the only named exception is Autism Project funds.

plain: Get DMH DD eligibility first.
Apply for MO HealthNet if the person does not have it.
Meet the support coordinator and make a plan together.
Ask the support coordinator to send the waiver request now, even with the wait list.
Tell the support coordinator in writing about every big change, for example a caregiver illness.
Keep a log of each call: the date, the name, and what was said.
pro: After eligibility, the Regional Office refers Medicaid enrollees to the county TCM provider. Families usually learn the provider from the eligibility letter.
The ISP is written with the family at least once a year. ICF/IID level of care is re-evaluated at least every 365 days for waiver users (DD Waiver Manual).
Ask the coordinator to submit the ISP, budget, and PON to Utilization Review now, so the wait list date starts (9 CSR 45-2.017(2)).
Ask in writing for a new PON when circumstances change (9 CSR 45-2.017(2)(B)).
Escalation: coordinator, then supervisor or agency director, then Regional Office Director, then DDD central office (573-751-4054), then DMH Constituent Services (1-800-364-9687).

bring: DD eligibility letter
MO HealthNet card or number
A list of the person's needs and goals
A dated log of calls and requests

wait.plain: The first plan is due within 30 business days after eligibility. It is due within 5 business days if the person needs services now.
wait.pro: ISP within 30 business days after eligibility; 5 business days for immediate need (9 CSR 45-2.010(4)).

plain: Without MO HealthNet, people in Greene, Henry, Laclede, Ozark, Stone, and Taney get only a state phone line.
Most new DD funding needs MO HealthNet.
There is no public list of support coordination agencies by county. Ask the Regional Office.
pro: Confirmed TCM providers: Greene, Abilities First The Next Step (417-886-0404); Stone, LinkAbility (417-334-8985); Lawrence, Lawrence County Case Management (417-678-6079, serves regardless of Medicaid); Webster, WC Partners (417-630-0782). Polk: Center for Human Services (secondary source). Other counties not confirmed.
Only the support coordinator submits the plan, budget, and PON to Utilization Review.

appeal.pro: Utilization Review decisions: regional director within 30 calendar days of the decision letter, or DSS fair hearing within 90 calendar days of written notice (9 CSR 45-2.017(9) to (11)).

name: DD waiver wait list and Priority of Need (PON)

summary.plain: When money is short, a score called PON decides who gets a DD waiver first. Get on the list early.
summary.pro: Access to DD waivers and general revenue Purchase of Service is ranked by Prioritization of Need (PON 1 to 5), then by time waiting (9 CSR 45-2.015, 2.017; DDD waiver enrollment page).

who.plain: People who are DD eligible and want waiver services. From 15 Oct 2026, new requests for 3 DD waivers go on a wait list.
who.pro: PON 1 to 4 comes from the MAAS (4 = highest need). PON 5 = verified emergency criteria (9 CSR 45-2.017(1)(E)): immediate need for life-sustaining services with no alternative to DDD funding; immediate need to protect self or others from imminent physical harm; living in an ICF/DD or nursing facility and able and wanting to move; lost significant waiver services due to age but still needs them; Children's Division custody with a funding agreement, or a Voluntary Placement Agreement. Emergency cases get the highest priority on the list (9 CSR 45-2.017(5)(C), (6)); that is a place on the list, not a slot. Ties go to the longest wait.

plain: Ask the support coordinator to send the plan, budget, and PON now.
Ask in writing for the PON score and the date the person joined the list.
Ask which waiver the person is listed for.
Tell the support coordinator in writing about every change, for example a hospital stay.
Ask for a new PON after each change.
Ask the support coordinator about other help while you wait.
In an emergency, tell the support coordinator in writing. Ask if the person meets the emergency criteria.
pro: The support coordinator submits the ISP, budget, and PON to Utilization Review (UR). UR reviews within 6 business days; the director decides within 5 business days, or within 5 business days after a 10-business-day request for more information; decision letter within 10 business days. Only the regional director or assistant regional director can deny or modify (9 CSR 45-2.017(1)(M), (7), (8)).
Request a new PON at each change in circumstances (9 CSR 45-2.017(2)(B)).

Emergency criteria give the highest priority on the list. The 15 Oct 2026 memo names no crisis, PON 5, or emergency exception. Ask the Regional Office Director in writing how an emergency case will be handled.

While waiting: State Plan services must be used first when they meet the need (9 CSR 45-2.017(14)(B)); SWMAP for autism; county SB40 funds; DD Health Home; DHSS home care (one HCBS waiver at a time, 9 CSR 45-2.015(5)).

wait.plain: There is no set end date. The rules give no time limit to move off the list.
wait.pro: No rule time limit to move from the list to a funded slot; funding and turnover decide. Turnover funds go first to current participants with increased needs (9 CSR 45-2.015(4)). The memo gives no estimated end date. The DDD page showed no wait list counts on 27 Oct 2026.

plain: An emergency puts a person at the top of the list. The memo does not say emergency cases skip the wait list.
Turning down an offered waiver can mean a new PON score.
For the children's MOCDD waiver, turning down a slot removes the child from the list.
A person can have only one waiver. A DHSS home care waiver blocks a DD waiver at the same time.
pro: Refusal of an offered slot: new PON (Comprehensive) or removal from the list (MOCDD) (9 CSR 45-2.015(3)(B)3, (3)(D)).
One HCBS waiver at a time, including other agencies' waivers (9 CSR 45-2.015(5)).
Loss of a primary caregiver counts under the rules when it happens, not when it is expected.

appeal.plain: If a request is denied, you can appeal within 30 days of the letter. See the appeals table.
appeal.pro: DMH track within 30 calendar days of the decision letter (9 CSR 45-2.017(9)); DSS fair hearing within 90 calendar days of written notice (9 CSR 45-2.017(10)(A)). No legal clock exists for moving off the wait list.

name: Comprehensive Waiver (DD)

summary.plain: This DD waiver pays for services, including support to live outside the family home, such as a group home.
summary.pro: 1915(c) DD waiver operated by DDD with the MO HealthNet Division. It is the only DD waiver with residential services (group home, shared living or host home, Individualized Supported Living).

who.plain: Children and adults who are DD eligible and have MO HealthNet. The person must need a lot of help in at least 3 life areas. The person needs support to live safely that the Community Support Waiver cannot give.
who.pro: DDD eligible; MO HealthNet in a federally matched category; ICF/IID level of care and at risk of ICF/IID placement; MAAS at least 95% below average in at least 3 major life areas (DD Waiver Eligibility sheet 09/2024); needs at least one waiver service each month; needs cannot be met in the Community Support Waiver and the person requires residential supports (DDD Waiver Fact Sheet, 22 Jan 2025). No individual annual cost cap.

plain: Get DMH DD eligibility and MO HealthNet.
Ask the support coordinator to request this waiver now.
Ask in writing for the PON score and the wait list date.
Ask the support coordinator about other help while you wait.
pro: The support coordinator submits the ISP, budget, and PON to Utilization Review (9 CSR 45-2.017).

When funding allows, priority goes to people who meet emergency criteria and need out-of-home residential care or whose needs exceed other waiver limits (9 CSR 45-2.015(3)(B)). Priority means a higher place on the list.
Waiver eligibility is determined within 60 days of a request (DDD Waiver Fact Sheet, 2025).

bring: DD eligibility letter
MO HealthNet number
Notes on daily care, safety, and supervision needs

wait.plain: New slots are on a wait list from 15 Oct 2026. There is no end date.
wait.pro: DDD memo, 15 Oct 2026: wait list for new enrollment due to budget limitations; no estimated end date; current participants continue; only Inter-Divisional Agreement cases and cases mandated by federal rule continue to enroll.

plain: Many families wait for a crisis. Ask for the request and PON now, before a crisis.
A person can be DD eligible but not meet waiver rules. Waivers need a lot of help in 3 areas.
A crisis can move the person higher on the list. It does not promise a waiver now.
pro: Loss of a primary caregiver counts under PON rules only when it happens.
One HCBS waiver at a time (9 CSR 45-2.015(5)).
Refusing an offered slot requires a new PON (9 CSR 45-2.015(3)(B)3).

appeal.plain: You can appeal a denial or cut. Ask the Regional Director within 30 days of the letter. Or ask MO HealthNet for a hearing within 90 days. To keep services, appeal before the change starts.
appeal.pro: DMH track: regional director within 30 calendar days of the decision letter; decision in 10 business days (9 CSR 45-2.017(9)). DSS track: written request within 90 calendar days of written notice to MO HealthNet Division, Constituent Services Unit, PO Box 6500, Jefferson City, MO 65102-6500, 1-800-392-2161 (9 CSR 45-2.017(10)(A)); starting the DSS appeal ends DMH appeal rights. Services under an existing ISP continue on a timely appeal; repayment is possible if the decision is upheld (9 CSR 45-2.017(11)). Federal rules tie continued services to an appeal before the date of action (42 CFR 431.230, 431.231): appeal before the change takes effect, and within 10 days of the notice if possible.

alert: 15 Oct 2026: DDD put new enrollment in this waiver on a wait list because of budget limits. There is no end date. People already on the waiver keep it. Still apply and get on the list. Ask the support coordinator about other help while you wait.

name: Community Support Waiver (DD)

summary.plain: This DD waiver pays for services for a person who lives with family or in their own home. The limit is $42,000 a year.
summary.pro: 1915(c) DD waiver for people with a home in the community; no residential services; annual waiver cost limit $42,000 per person, which may be exceeded case by case.

who.plain: Children and adults who are DD eligible and have MO HealthNet. The person must need a lot of help in at least 3 life areas. The person lives in the community, usually with family.
who.pro: DDD eligible; MO HealthNet; ICF/IID level of care; 3 or more major life areas (DD Waiver Eligibility sheet 09/2024); needs at least one waiver service monthly; annual cost limit $42,000 per person, may be exceeded case by case (DDD Waiver Fact Sheet 22 Jan 2025; DD Waiver Manual 1.5 and 1.9, file 2026/09).

plain: Get DMH DD eligibility and MO HealthNet.
Ask the support coordinator to request this waiver now.
Ask in writing for the PON score and the wait list date.
List the services the person needs most, for example respite or job help.
pro: Services include in-home and out-of-home respite, personal assistant (self-direction option; Electronic Visit Verification required), day habilitation, career planning, job development, supported employment, prevocational services, benefits planning, home-delivered meals, crisis intervention, OT, PT, and speech therapy, assistive technology, home and vehicle modifications, remote supports, specialized medical equipment and supplies, support broker, and transportation.
OT, PT, and speech through the waiver can continue after age 21, when MO HealthNet State Plan therapy stops (DD Waiver Manual).

wait.plain: New slots are on a wait list from 15 Oct 2026. There is no end date.
wait.pro: DDD memo, 15 Oct 2026: wait list for new enrollment; no estimated end date; current participants continue; exceptions only for Inter-Divisional Agreement cases and cases mandated by federal rule.

plain: The yearly limit is $42,000 for each person. It can be raised case by case.
This waiver does not pay for a place to live, such as a group home.
A person can have only one waiver at a time.
pro: One HCBS waiver at a time (9 CSR 45-2.015(5)).
State Plan services must be used first when they meet the need (9 CSR 45-2.017(14)(B)).

appeal.plain: You can appeal a denial or cut. Ask the Regional Director within 30 days of the letter. Or ask MO HealthNet for a hearing within 90 days. To keep services, appeal before the change starts.
appeal.pro: DMH track: 30 calendar days from the decision letter (9 CSR 45-2.017(9)). DSS track: 90 calendar days from written notice, MO HealthNet Division, Constituent Services Unit, PO Box 6500, Jefferson City, MO 65102-6500, 1-800-392-2161; starting it ends DMH appeal rights (9 CSR 45-2.017(10)(A)). Services continue on a timely appeal; repayment possible (9 CSR 45-2.017(11)). Appeal before the effective date, and within 10 days if possible (42 CFR 431.230, 431.231).

alert: 15 Oct 2026: DDD put new enrollment in this waiver on a wait list because of budget limits. There is no end date. People already on the waiver keep it. Still apply and get on the list. Ask the support coordinator about other help while you wait.

name: Partnership for Hope Waiver (DD)

summary.plain: This smaller DD waiver pays for services up to a yearly limit. County DD boards help pay for it.
summary.pro: County-based 1915(c) DD waiver; no residential services; cap $12,362 a year (up to $15,000 in special circumstances); the state share is split equally with local SB40 boards.

who.plain: Children and adults who are DD eligible and have MO HealthNet. The person must need a lot of help in at least 3 life areas. Needs must fit within $12,362 a year. The person must live in a county that takes part. Douglas and Wright counties do not take part.
who.pro: DDD eligible; MO HealthNet; ICF/IID level of care (3 or more areas); needs met within $12,362 a year, up to $15,000 in special circumstances (DDD Waiver Fact Sheet 2025); manual exceptions up to $10,000 one-time (crisis or transition) or up to $3,000 a year ongoing, approved jointly by the County Board Director, regional director, and DD Deputy or Assistant Director (DD Waiver Manual 1.8, file 2026/09); no residential services; lives in a participating county; meets crisis or priority criteria (9 CSR 45-2.015(3)(A)). PfH operates where the SB40 board has authorized funds or in a CMS-approved county (9 CSR 45-2.015(1)(G)). DDD map (Sept 2025): all 23 counties except Douglas and Wright. The SB40 board determines each applicant's category (DD Waiver Manual).

plain: Get DMH DD eligibility and MO HealthNet.
Ask the support coordinator to request this waiver now.
Ask in writing for the wait list date.
Ask the county DD board about help while you wait.
pro: Crisis criteria: serious risk of immediate harm or death; loss of primary caregiver or caregiver cannot meet needs; abuse, neglect, or exploitation (9 CSR 45-2.015(3)(A)). The 15 Oct 2026 memo names no crisis exception to the wait list.

Priority criteria, by time waiting: needs substantial accommodation the caregiver cannot provide; has used up school and Vocational Rehabilitation benefits (or is not VR eligible) and needs employment services; has had county-funded supports for 3 months or more that the waiver can cover; leaving a non-Medicaid residential care facility.
Services unique to PfH: dental, family peer support, temporary residential services. Respite is not in PfH (Fact Sheet 2025).

wait.plain: New slots are on a wait list from 15 Oct 2026. There is no end date.
wait.pro: DDD memo, 15 Oct 2026: wait list for new enrollment; no estimated end date; current participants continue; exceptions only for Inter-Divisional Agreement cases and cases mandated by federal rule.

plain: People in Douglas and Wright counties cannot use this waiver.
This waiver does not pay for respite.
Help from the county DD board for 3 months or more can raise priority.
A person who has used up school and VR job help can get priority for job services.
pro: The 9 CSR 45-2.015(1)(G) rule does not require a board to fund half; the equal split comes from the DDD fact sheet (fact check, 27 Oct 2026).
One HCBS waiver at a time (9 CSR 45-2.015(5)).

appeal.pro: DMH track: 30 calendar days from the decision letter (9 CSR 45-2.017(9)). who.plain: Adults 18 and older with a disability, people who are blind, and people 65 and older. Children use other MO HealthNet groups. In 2026, the income limit without a spend down is $1,131 a month for one person. The savings limit is $6,220.50 for one person.

who.plain: People on MO HealthNet for disability whose income is over $1,131 a month in 2026. This often happens with SSDI or Childhood Disability Benefits.
who.pro: MHABD with countable income above $1,131 single (2026). Spend down = countable income minus the limit. Coverage for each month the spend down is met; up to a year back can be met.

Option 1: pay the amount to MO HealthNet before the 1st of the month. Then you have coverage all month.

Ask FSD if Adult Expansion, Ticket to Work Health Assurance, or a waiver would cost less.

name: SSI (Supplemental Security Income)

summary.plain: SSI is a monthly payment from Social Security for people with disabilities who have little income and savings.
summary.pro: Title XVI needs-based cash benefit for aged, blind, or disabled people with limited income and resources.

who.plain: Children and adults with a disability or blindness, and people 65 or older. Savings must be $2,000 or less for one person. In 2026, SSI pays up to $994 a month. In 2027, it pays up to $1,029.
who.pro: FBR 2026 $994 individual, $1,491 couple; 2027 $1,029 and $1,544 (POMS SI 02001.020). Resources $2,000 individual, $3,000 couple (20 CFR 416.1205). $20 general exclusion; $65 plus half of remaining earnings excluded; unearned income (SSDI, CDB) reduces SSI dollar for dollar after $20. Missouri pays no state supplement to people living independently. Parent deeming through the month the child turns 18 (20 CFR 416.1165). Student earned income exclusion (under 22, regularly in school): 2026 $2,410 a month, $9,730 a year; 2027 $2,500 and $10,080 (POMS SI 00820.510).

plain: Contact Social Security to apply. The first contact sets the filing date.
Gather medical records, school records, and a list of all doctors.
If the person lives with family, write a rent agreement.
Apply for MO HealthNet too. In Missouri, SSI does not bring it.
Report wages to Social Security by the 6th of the next month.
pro: Apply by phone, at a field office, or online at ssa.gov for some adult claims; child SSI needs an interview. The first contact sets a protective filing date.
The person must file for other benefits they may get, for example CDB.

ISM (rules since 30 Sep 2024): only shelter counts, not food. Rent at least the PMV ($351.33 in 2026; $363.00 in 2027) avoids ISM. The one-third reduction (VTR: $331.33 in 2026) applies only if the person lives in another's household, gets shelter there, and others provide all meals. A household member on SNAP or other need-based aid makes it a public assistance household with no ISM from household members (20 CFR 416.1130, 416.1142).
Apply separately to FSD for MHABD (Missouri 209(b)).

bring: Birth certificate and Social Security number
Proof of citizenship or immigration status
Bank statements
Lease or written rent agreement
Pay stubs
IEP, 504 plan, and school records
Medical records and the names of all doctors and clinics

plain: Savings over $2,000 on the 1st of the month stop SSI for that month. An ABLE account can help.
Free rent from family can lower SSI. Food no longer counts.
If someone in the home gets SNAP, free rent does not lower SSI.
Report wages on time, or you may owe money back.
pro: POMS SI 00835.020 still lists food as ISM; the regulation (20 CFR 416.1130, effective 30 Sep 2024) controls.
SSI ends when Title II income reaches FBR plus $20 (2026: $1,014).

appeal.plain: Appeal within 60 days of the date on the letter. To keep payments during the appeal, appeal within 10 days of that date.
appeal.pro: Reconsideration, ALJ hearing, Appeals Council, federal court: 60 days after receipt at each level, receipt presumed 5 days after the notice date (20 CFR 416.1401, 416.1409, 416.1433, 416.1468, 422.210(c)). Payments continue if the appeal is filed within 10 days after receipt (416.1336(b)); continued payments may become an overpayment if the person loses, and continuation can be waived in writing (416.1336(c)). Counting from the notice date gives the shorter, safer period.

name: SSI at age 18 (adult rules and the age 18 review)

summary.plain: At 18, Social Security reviews SSI using adult rules. Some young adults can apply for the first time.
summary.pro: Age 18 redetermination under adult initial disability rules (20 CFR 416.987), end of parent deeming (416.1165), and Section 301 continuation (416.1338).

who.plain: Teens turning 18 who get SSI now. Also teens who could not get SSI before because of their parents' income.
who.pro: Child SSI recipients are redetermined within one year after the 18th birthday under the adult initial disability standard; medical improvement rules and the SGA step do not apply (POMS DI 23570.020). Parent deeming stops after the month of the 18th birthday; a new adult claim can be filed for the next month. Section 301: if found not disabled, payments can continue if the person began, before the disability ended, an IEP (age 18 to 21), a VR Individualized Plan for Employment, or a Ticket to Work plan; for an IEP student 18 to 21, SSA will find that continuing helps.

plain: At 16 or 17, gather medical and school records.
Keep the young adult's savings at $2,000 or less from the month after the 18th birthday.
If the young adult will live with family, write a rent agreement.
In the birthday month, call Social Security to set a filing date for adult SSI.
If the young adult gets SSI now, answer every Social Security letter on time.
If the young adult has an IEP or a VR plan, tell Social Security.
pro: Rent at or above the PMV ($363.00 a month in 2027) avoids an ISM reduction.
Open an ABLE account before savings reach $2,000.
Show SSA the IEP, VR IPE, or Ticket plan for Section 301 continuation (20 CFR 416.1338).

plain: Savings in the young adult's name, such as gifts, can block SSI.
Free rent from family can lower SSI. A rent agreement helps.
Many families do not know an IEP or VR plan can keep payments going.
pro: Families often have only old medical evidence; SSA uses adult rules at 18.

appeal.plain: If Social Security says no, appeal within 10 days of the date on the letter to keep payments. You have 60 days to appeal at all.
appeal.pro: 60 days after receipt (receipt presumed 5 days after the notice date); continuation if filed within 10 days after receipt (20 CFR 416.1336(b), 416.1409).

summary.plain: SSDI pays people who worked and paid Social Security taxes, then became disabled.
summary.pro: Title II disability insurance benefits based on the worker's own insured status.

who.plain: Adults with enough work history who cannot do substantial work because of a disability. In 2026, substantial work means earning over $1,690 a month. In 2027, it is $1,770.
who.pro: Insured status and disability under SSA rules. SGA non-blind 2026 $1,690, 2027 $1,770; blind 2026 $2,830, 2027 $2,950 (POMS DI 10501.015). Trial work period service month 2026 $1,210, 2027 $1,270; 9 service months in a rolling 60 months (POMS DI 13010.060). Medicare after 24 months of entitlement. Five-month waiting period and extended period of eligibility: standard rules, not re-checked.

plain: Apply online, by phone, or at a Social Security office.
Gather work history and medical records.
Before taking a job, get free benefits counseling.
Report work to Social Security.
pro: Get a Benefits Planning Query (BPQY) and a WIPA analysis before work starts.
When Medicare starts, apply for MSP; Adult Expansion ends.

plain: SSDI over $1,131 a month can cause a MO HealthNet spend down.
SSDI can lower or end SSI.
Medicare starts after 24 months. Apply for a Medicare Savings Program then.
pro: Title II income reduces SSI dollar for dollar after $20; SSI ends at FBR plus $20 (2026: $1,014).

appeal.plain: Appeal within 60 days of the date on the letter. If SSDI stops for health reasons, ask within 10 days to keep payments.
appeal.pro: 60 days after receipt at each level (20 CFR 404 and 416 parallel rules; 422.210(c)); receipt presumed 5 days after the notice date. Medical cessation: elect continued benefits within 10 days after receipt (20 CFR 404.1597a(f), (g)).

name: Childhood Disability Benefits (CDB, also called DAC)

summary.plain: CDB pays an adult who was disabled before age 22, from a parent's Social Security record.
summary.pro: Title II child's benefits for an adult disabled before 22 (Disabled Adult Child), on a parent's record.

who.plain: Adults 18 or older whose disability began before age 22. A parent must get Social Security retirement or disability, or have died after working. The adult child usually must not be married.
who.pro: Parent entitled to retirement or disability benefits, or died fully or currently insured; adult child unmarried, dependent, and disabled before 22. Marriage ends CDB except marriage to a Title II beneficiary (not a child under 18 or a student child aged 18 or 19); marriage to an SSI-only spouse ends it. Re-entitlement any time if CDB ended because of SGA work; within 84 months if it ended for medical improvement; marriage since last entitlement blocks re-entitlement. SGA applies (2026 $1,690; 2027 $1,770). Medicare Part A after 24 months (POMS RS 00203.001, .015, .035).

plain: When a parent files for retirement or disability, ask Social Security about CDB for the adult child.
Ask again if a parent dies.
Bring proof the disability began before 22, such as school and early medical records.
If CDB ends SSI, tell FSD in writing. Ask FSD to keep MO HealthNet under DAC rules.
pro: DAC Medicaid protection (Section 1634(c)): a CDB beneficiary who lost SSI because of CDB entitlement or an increase (on or after 1 Jul 1987), and would still get SSI without it, must be treated as an SSI recipient for Medicaid (POMS SI 01715.015). How FSD applies this in Missouri is not public.
When Medicare starts, apply for MSP.

bring: Parent's Social Security number
Proof of relationship, such as a birth certificate
School and medical records that show the disability began before 22

plain: Marriage can end CDB for good. Talk to a benefits counselor before marriage.
CDB often replaces SSI. MO HealthNet can be protected, but you must tell FSD.
Families often miss CDB when a parent retires early, at 62.
pro: CDB above $1,131 (2026) creates an MHABD spend down unless DAC protection is applied.

appeal.plain: Appeal within 60 days of the date on the letter. If CDB stops for health reasons, ask within 10 days to keep payments.
appeal.pro: 60 days after receipt; medical cessation continuation within 10 days after receipt (20 CFR 404.1597a).

name: Working while on SSI, SSDI, or CDB (work incentives)

summary.plain: Special rules let people work and keep some benefits and health coverage. Get free benefits counseling first.
summary.pro: SSA work incentives (1619(a), 1619(b), PASS, IRWE, BWE, student exclusion, TWP, EPE) and WIPA benefits counseling through the Ticket to Work Help Line.

who.plain: People who get SSI, SSDI, or Childhood Disability Benefits and work or want to work. Counseling serves ages 14 and older.
who.pro: SSI: earnings reduce SSI about $1 for each $2 after $85; 1619(a) keeps cash above SGA until break-even; 1619(b) keeps Medicaid when gross earnings are under the Missouri threshold, 2026 $55,181 a year (POMS SI 02302.200), with resources at or under $2,000 and Medicaid in the month before 1619 status (209(b) rule, POMS SI 01715.015). PASS, IRWE, BWE, and the student exclusion (under 22) apply. SSDI and CDB: TWP month 2026 $1,210, 2027 $1,270; SGA 2026 $1,690, 2027 $1,770 (blind $2,830, $2,950); CDB re-entitlement any time if it ended for SGA. WIPA serves beneficiaries 14 to full retirement age; Ticket to Work serves 18 to 64.

plain: Before a job starts, call the Ticket to Work Help Line at 1-866-968-7842.
Ask for benefits counseling.
Ask Social Security for a Benefits Planning Query. It lists the person's benefits.
Report pay to Social Security every month.
Keep pay stubs and receipts for work costs.
Put savings in an ABLE account to stay under the SSI limit.
pro: The Help Line routes callers to the WIPA project for their ZIP code.
PASS needs form SSA-545 and SSA approval.
Tell FSD about 1619(b) status so MO HealthNet is not closed.

plain: We found no benefits counseling project based in Southwest Missouri. The Help Line will route you.
Many families fear losing Medicaid and turn down work. Rules like 1619(b) can protect it.
In 2026, MO HealthNet can continue with yearly pay up to $55,181 under 1619(b).
pro: Paraquad's WIPA service area excludes SW Missouri; which WIPA project serves Greene County is not verified.
2027 Missouri 1619(b) threshold not yet published.

contacts.label: Ticket to Work Help Line (benefits counseling)
contacts.note: TTY 1-866-833-2967. Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern.

name: ABLE account (MO ABLE)

summary.plain: An ABLE account lets a person with a disability save money without losing SSI or MO HealthNet.
summary.pro: Tax-advantaged account under 26 USC 529A; excluded for SSI up to $100,000 and fully excluded for Medicaid.

who.plain: People whose disability began before age 46. This changed in 2026. Before 2026, the age was 26.
who.pro: Onset before age 46 from 1 Jan 2026 (was 26) (26 USC 529A(e)). One account per person. Eligible by SSI or SSDI receipt based on that disability, or by a disability certification.

plain: Check that the disability began before age 46.
Open an account online with MO ABLE or another state's ABLE plan.
Have the Social Security award letter, or a signed disability statement, ready.
Move savings into the account before they reach $2,000.
Spend money for housing in the same month you take it out.
pro: 2026 contribution limit $20,000 from all sources (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.34); 2027 limit not yet published.
ABLE to Work: a working owner with no employer retirement contributions may add earnings up to the lesser of earnings or the prior-year one-person poverty line ($15,650 in 2026).

SSI: first $100,000 excluded; if only the excess over $100,000 puts the person over $2,000, SSI is suspended but Medicaid continues. Non-housing distributions are excluded while kept for the expense; housing distributions kept into the next month count (POMS SI 01130.740).
Missouri income tax subtraction for contributions up to $8,000 (single) or $16,000 (married filing combined) (Missouri DOR FAQ; check the current form).
Medicaid payback at death may apply after qualified expenses; MO HealthNet practice not confirmed.

cost: Plan fees apply. MO ABLE fees were not checked.

plain: Many families think ABLE is only for disability before 26. That changed in 2026.
Deposits from everyone together can total $20,000 in 2026.
Money for rent must be spent in the same month you take it out.
Wages put into ABLE still count as income for SSI.
pro: Third-party contributions are not income to the owner; wages deposited directly still count as earned income.

alert: 1 Jan 2026: The age limit rose from 26 to 46. More people can now open an ABLE account.

name: Special needs trusts (first-party, pooled, and family trusts)

summary.plain: A special needs trust holds money for a person with a disability. It can protect SSI and MO HealthNet.
summary.pro: First-party (42 USC 1396p(d)(4)(A)), pooled (d)(4)(C), and third-party supplemental needs trusts.

who.plain: People with a disability who have or will get money, such as back pay, a settlement, or an inheritance. Also parents and grandparents who are planning their wills.
who.pro: First-party: established before 65 for the disabled person's own assets; sole benefit; Medicaid payback with the state as first payee; since 13 Dec 2016 the person may set it up (POMS SI 01120.203). Pooled: Missouri Family Trust, operating as Midwest Special Needs Trust (RSMo 402.199 to 402.208); at death 25% of principal to the charitable trust, then Medicaid payback (402.203); state agencies disregard the account for Chapter 208 programs unless federal law prohibits it (402.199); a transfer at 65 or older may cause a penalty. Third-party: family money, no payback; cash to the beneficiary is SSI income; shelter payments are ISM (POMS SI 01120.200, not re-opened).

plain: Do not leave money in the person's own name.
Name a trust or an ABLE account in wills, life insurance, and retirement plans.
If the person gets a lump sum, talk to a lawyer before it is spent or saved.
For small amounts, ask a lawyer or the FSD worker about a pooled trust.
pro: Submit a funded first-party or pooled trust to SSA and FSD for review.

cost: Lawyer fees. Pooled trust fees were not checked.

plain: Cash given straight to the person counts as income for SSI.
Trust payments for rent can lower SSI.
A first-party trust must be set up before age 65.
Grandparents often leave money to the person directly. This can end SSI and MO HealthNet.
pro: Midwest Special Needs Trust contact details came from a secondary source and were not verified; they are omitted here.

name: SNAP (food assistance)

summary.plain: SNAP gives money each month to buy food. Households with a disabled member have easier rules.
summary.pro: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program run by FSD under USDA rules; special rules for households with an elderly (60+) or disabled member.

who.plain: Households with low income. From 1 Oct 2026, one person can have net income up to $1,330 a month. If no one is disabled or 60 or older, gross income must also be $1,729 or less.
who.pro: FY2027 (1 Oct 2026 to 30 Sep 2027, USDA): 1 person gross $1,729, net $1,330 a month; 2 people gross $2,345, net $1,804. The DSS chart dated 10/01/2026 still shows the FY2026 figures ($1,696 and $1,305); use the USDA figures. Households with an elderly or disabled member meet only the net test (7 CFR 273.9(a)), have no excess shelter cap, and may deduct medical costs over $35 a month, including the MO HealthNet spend down. Resources $3,000, or $4,750 with a member 60+ or disabled. Maximum allotment, 1 person: $306. A disabled member includes an SSI or Social Security disability recipient (7 CFR 271.2). A person under 22 living with a parent is in the parent's household (7 CFR 273.1(b)(1)(ii)).

plain: Apply online at mydss.mo.gov, or call 855-373-4636.
Do the phone interview. If you miss it, call 855-823-4908.
Send receipts for medical costs over $35 a month.
Answer every renewal letter on time.
pro: Apply online, by mail to FSD, P.O. Box 2700, Jefferson City, MO 65102, or by fax 573-526-9400.
Work rules from 1 Nov 2025 apply to able-bodied adults; exemptions include a physical or mental health reason and caring for someone who needs help with self-care.

wait.plain: FSD decides within 30 days. Some households get food help within 7 days.
wait.pro: Normal processing within 30 days; expedited in 7 days or less for some households.

plain: A young adult under 22 who lives with a parent must be in the parent's SNAP case.
Report medical costs to get a bigger benefit.
When someone in the home gets SNAP, free rent does not lower SSI.
The DSS income chart was out of date in October 2026. Ask FSD to use the new limits.
pro: The DSS chart also has typing errors (for example, the same net figure for 4 and 5 people). Do not copy it without a check.

appeal.plain: Ask for a hearing within 90 days of the date on the Action Notice. To keep benefits during the hearing, ask within 10 days of that date.
appeal.pro: DSS hearings page: 90 days from the date shown on the Action Notice; within 10 days to keep benefits.

alert: Oct 2026: The DSS income chart still shows last year's SNAP limits. The new limits from 1 Oct 2026 are higher. Apply even if the old chart says no.

sources.title: USDA FNS, SNAP FY 2027 cost-of-living adjustments
DSS Benefit Program Income Limits (stale SNAP row)

name: Blind Pension and Supplemental Aid to the Blind

summary.plain: Missouri pays monthly cash and MO HealthNet to some adults who are blind.
summary.pro: Missouri Blind Pension (BP) and Supplemental Aid to the Blind (SAB), run by FSD; both include MO HealthNet.

who.plain: Adults 18 and older who are blind under Missouri law. Missouri counts a person as blind in two ways. Sight in the better eye is 5/200 or worse with glasses. Or side vision is 5 degrees or less, called tunnel vision. Blind Pension is for people who cannot get SSI. Supplemental Aid to the Blind adds to SSI.
who.pro: Blindness (RSMo 209.040): central acuity that cannot be corrected to better than 5/200 in the better eye, OR a visual field of 5 degrees or less in the better eye; lasting or expected to last 12 months; certified by an ophthalmologist, a physician skilled in eye disease, or an optometrist designated or approved by DSS. BP (2026): grant $949 a month (Appendix K 07/2026; effective date not printed); resources up to $29,999 (home exempt); no income limit for the blind person; sighted spouse income under $9,017 a month; not eligible for SSI or SAB; no valid driver license; not in a public or medical institution; moral character form required. SAB: applies for or gets SSI; income other than SSI not over $1,073 a month (1 Jan 2026); grant = $949 minus SSI; resources $6,220.50 single, $12,441 couple (1 Jul 2026); federally matched MO HealthNet with no spend down.

plain: Get an eye exam report that gives both sharpness of sight and field of vision.
Apply for MO HealthNet and ask for Blind Pension or Supplemental Aid to the Blind.
If the person has MO HealthNet now, file an addendum instead.
Call the Blind Service Center at 866-877-8155 with questions.
pro: Apply through the MO HealthNet application or an addendum: mydssupload.mo.gov; FSD, P.O. Box 2700, Jefferson City, MO 65102; fax 573-526-9400; or an FSD Resource Center.
Rehabilitation Services for the Blind does not handle BP or SAB.

bring: Eye exam report with sight and field of vision
Proof of savings and property
Social Security letters, if any

plain: Missouri's rule is stricter than Social Security's. A person can be blind for SSA but not for Missouri.
Tunnel vision can qualify. Make sure the eye report includes field of vision.
Blind Pension can help a person whose SSDI is too high for SSI.
Blind Pension allows savings up to $29,999.
The person cannot drive or hold a driver license.
pro: File 06 gave only the 5/200 route; the fact check added the visual field route (RSMo 209.040).

appeal.plain: Ask FSD for a hearing within 90 days of the notice date. Ask within 10 days to keep benefits.
appeal.pro: FSD hearing: 90 days from the Action Notice date; within 10 days to keep benefits (DSS hearings page).

summary.plain: With supported decision-making, the person makes their own choices with help from people they trust.
summary.pro: A supported decision-making (SDM) agreement is a less restrictive alternative that a Missouri court must consider before guardianship (RSMo 475.075.13).

who.plain: Any adult who can make decisions with help. Families can start planning before age 18.
who.pro: No Missouri statute defines SDM or sets a form; RSMo 475.010 has no definition (based on the sources checked). RSMo 475.075.13 (added by SB 806, 2018) lists supported decision-making agreements among alternatives the court shall consider. No statute requires third parties to honor an SDM agreement. Combine with FERPA and HIPAA releases, a durable POA, and an SSA representative payee.

plain: Talk with the person about which decisions they want help with.
Choose supporters the person trusts.
Write down the agreement. The person signs it.
Sign releases so supporters can talk with doctors, banks, and schools.
At the IEP meeting before 18, plan how the student will get help with school decisions.
pro: IDEA rights transfer to the student at 18 unless a court has declared the student incompetent (DESE Regulation V, section L; 34 CFR 300.520). The IEP must note the transfer at least one year before 18 (34 CFR 300.320(c)).
An adult student can sign a release or invite a parent to IEP meetings; an SDM agreement can name the parent as a supporter.

plain: No Missouri law makes hospitals, banks, or schools accept the agreement. Add releases and a power of attorney.
At 18, school rights move to the student. A parent has no say unless the student includes them.
Some schools, hospitals, and banks tell families they need guardianship. The law says courts must consider other options first.
pro: No Missouri appellate decision applying supported decision-making was found (CourtListener, 26 Oct 2026).

sources.title: ICI Impact, Supported Decision-Making: The Missouri Approach (secondary)

name: Power of attorney and health care power of attorney

summary.plain: A power of attorney lets the person choose someone to handle money or health decisions. It can avoid guardianship.
summary.pro: Durable power of attorney (RSMo 404.700 to 404.737) and durable power of attorney for health care (404.800 to 404.872).

who.plain: Adults who understand what they are signing. The person must sign while they can still make the choice.
who.pro: A financial POA is durable only if titled Durable Power of Attorney, contains the statutory durability sentence, and is signed, dated, and acknowledged like a real estate deed, that is, notarized (RSMo 404.705.1). Health care powers start when two licensed physicians certify incapacity unless the document says otherwise (404.825). Authority to withdraw artificially supplied nutrition and hydration must be granted specifically (404.820). The guardianship court gives weight to a DPOA signed before the petition (475.075.13). No Missouri rule sets a capacity test for signing a POA (sources checked).

plain: Talk with the person about who should help.
Ask a lawyer or legal aid to help write the documents.
Sign the documents in front of a notary.
Give copies to doctors, the bank, and the person chosen to help.
Do this before anyone files for guardianship.
pro: Appointment of a guardian revokes an earlier health care POA unless the court orders otherwise (RSMo 475.361.3). Choose the order of documents with care.

cost: Notary fee. Lawyer fees if you use a lawyer.

plain: Banks and doctors sometimes refuse a power of attorney.
If someone doubts the person understands, get advice first.
A later guardianship cancels a health care power of attorney unless the court says otherwise.

summary.plain: A representative payee gets and manages a person's Social Security money for them.
summary.pro: SSA payee for SSI (20 CFR 416.601 to 416.665) and Title II (404.2001 and following).

who.plain: People who get SSI, SSDI, or Childhood Disability Benefits and need help managing that money.
who.pro: SSA decides whether a payee serves the person's interest. Use of a payee and choice of payee are appealable initial determinations (20 CFR 416.1402(d), (e)). SSA must give advance written notice naming the payee and explaining appeal rights (416.630(a)). Courts must consider an existing payee as a less restrictive alternative to conservatorship (RSMo 475.075.13(3)).

plain: Ask Social Security about a representative payee.
Keep records of how the money is spent.
If you disagree with the payee choice, appeal within 10 days of the letter.
pro: A protest or appeal within 10 days after receiving the mailed notice delays the appointment until a decision (20 CFR 416.630(b)(2)).

plain: A payee covers only Social Security money. It does not cover health care, bank accounts, or contracts.
A payee plus an ABLE account may avoid a conservatorship.

appeal.plain: Appeal within 60 days. Appeal within 10 days to delay the payee choice.
appeal.pro: 60 days after receipt (416.1409); 10 days to delay appointment (416.630(b)(2)).

name: Guardianship and conservatorship (probate court)

summary.plain: A guardian is a person a court picks to make decisions for an adult. The court must look at other options first.
summary.pro: Adult guardianship and conservatorship under RSMo Chapter 475, filed in the probate division of the county of residence.

who.plain: Adults the court finds cannot make or share key decisions, even with help. A limited guardianship covers only some decisions. A conservator handles money and property.
who.pro: Incapacity: unable to receive and evaluate information or communicate decisions to the extent that the person cannot meet essential needs so that serious physical injury, illness, or disease is likely (RSMo 475.010, 475.075.11). Clear and convincing evidence (475.075.9). Before appointing, the court shall consider less restrictive alternatives: a DPOA signed before the petition, a trust, a representative payee, supported decision-making agreements, services or assistive technology, an emergency guardian ad litem, or a limited guardian (475.075.13). Limited guardianship for partial incapacity, listing specific powers (475.080). The order must address supervised living, finances, and the rights to vote, drive, and marry (475.075.14). Conservatorship for financial disability (475.010); bond and annual settlements apply.

plain: First try other options: supported decision-making, a power of attorney, or a payee.
If a guardian is still needed, talk to a lawyer.
File a petition in the probate court of the county where the person lives.
Ask for a limited guardianship that lists only the powers needed.
File the yearly report the court requires.
pro: Any person may petition (475.060); the petition must state facts and specific behaviors showing the need. The court may order an examination (475.075.6), appoints a lawyer for the respondent at once (475.075.4), and requires personal service (475.075.2). Venue: county of residence (475.035).
Respondent rights: counsel, jury, presence, silence, evidence, cross-examination, open or closed hearing, appeal (475.075.10).
Emergency guardian ad litem: hearing within 5 business days, appointment up to 90 days (475.075.15).
Annual reports for life (475.082). The ward may petition at any time to restore rights (475.083.4).
Greene County Probate Division: attorneys filing adult cases are responsible for service on the respondent.

wait.plain: No set time for a regular hearing. An emergency hearing can happen within 5 business days.
wait.pro: No statutory deadline for a regular hearing; emergency GAL hearing within 5 business days (475.075.15).

cost: Court costs, the fee of the person's court-appointed lawyer, and any exam fee. Call the court to confirm the amount.

plain: Schools, hospitals, and banks may say you need guardianship at 18. The law says to look at other options first.
Full guardianship removes rights the person might keep with a limited order.
Guardianship lasts until a court ends it. Reports are due every year.
A guardianship cancels a health care power of attorney unless the court says otherwise.
pro: Greene County fee amounts are not confirmed; the clerk's fee page layout does not show which line the advance deposit belongs to (fact check). Do not quote a cost.
Ward rights (475.361) include the least restrictive form of guardianship and restoration at the earliest possible time.

appeal.plain: The person can appeal. The deadline is short. Talk to the court-appointed lawyer right away. The person can also ask the court later to give back rights.
appeal.pro: Notice of appeal within 10 days after the judgment becomes final, usually 30 days after entry (Mo. Sup. Ct. Rules 81.04, 81.05; secondary summary, not verified). Restoration: any time, even by informal letter (475.083.4); a contested petition not more than once every 180 days (475.083.6).

name: Disability civil rights complaints (ADA, Section 504, fair housing)

summary.plain: Federal law forbids unfair treatment because of disability by public programs, funded programs, and landlords.
summary.pro: ADA Title II, Section 504, the Olmstead integration mandate, and the Fair Housing Act reasonable accommodation rule.

who.plain: Anyone treated unfairly because of a disability by a government program, a program that gets federal money, or a landlord. This includes people at risk of going into an institution because services are missing.
who.pro: Olmstead v. L.C., 527 U.S. 581 (1999): unjustified institutional isolation is discrimination. Hiltibran v. Levy, 793 F. Supp. 2d 1108 (W.D. Mo. 2011): people at risk of institutionalization may bring integration claims. Fair housing: refusal of reasonable accommodations is unlawful (24 CFR 100.204). A.J.T. v. Osseo Area Schools, 605 U.S. 335 (2025): school ADA and 504 claims do not need bad faith or gross misjudgment. A Title II or 504 lawsuit does not require an administrative complaint first.

plain: Write down what happened and when.
Call Mo P&A for advice.
For a government program, file a complaint within 180 days.
For housing, file with HUD within 1 year.
pro: ADA Title II administrative complaint within 180 days unless extended for good cause (28 CFR 35.170(b)). HUD complaint within 1 year (42 USC 3610(a)(1)(A)(i)); fair housing suit within 2 years (42 USC 3613(a)(1)(A)). Missouri Commission on Human Rights: verified complaint within 180 days (RSMo 213.075.1; housing filing rules not checked).
